source_user: Advanced cluster case RDMA-1: Explain how RDMA changes the data path for multi-node GPU training or inference. Variant 1 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate verbs, queues, memory registration, transport selection, bandwidth, latency, and fallback behavior; compare measured device counters with application-level communication time. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: Implement an RDMA data-path explanation for multi-node GPU training or inference (Variant 1), explicitly distinguishing model-domain mechanisms from measured runtime behavior. State assumptions without inventing NIC, topology, driver, or framework facts. Explain the path from application collective or point-to-point operation through the communication library and verbs layer (queues, work requests/completions, memory registration, protection/access requirements) to transport selection, NIC/link, and remote memory/GPU effects; contrast RDMA with the relevant fallback path and identify where copies, synchronization, and CPU involvement may occur. Define a falsifiable hypothesis with a named baseline and workload: specify topology and software/hardware versions as variables to record, message-size/batch/parallelism distribution, warm-up and steady-state windows, repetitions, and units. Measure application communication time and overlap/utilization alongside device counters, bandwidth, latency, queue/completion errors, retransmissions or link events where available, and GPU step time; do not infer end-to-end improvement from a single counter. Report distributions (including p50/p95/p99 where relevant), confidence/variability, and confounders such as topology, message size, contention, registration/cache effects, synchronization, clocking, and fallback activation. Include a minimal comparison matrix for RDMA and fallback, deterministic reproduction steps, and a rollback condition: disable/revert RDMA or isolate the link if correctness checks fail, error rates rise, tail latency or step time breaches a predeclared threshold, or fallback is not healthy. Treat measurements as evidence rather than guarantees; redact workload-identifying payloads and restrict telemetry access.

quality_dimensions.correctness: rewrite: separates RDMA mechanisms, fallback, and measured end-to-end effects
quality_dimensions.completeness: rewrite: adds assumptions, hypothesis, metrics, confounders, failure/rollback criteria, and safety limits
quality_dimensions.clarity: rewrite: requires an explicit data-path narrative and comparison matrix
quality_dimensions.testability: rewrite: specifies reproducible workload, baseline, windows, distributions, and predeclared thresholds

risks: RDMA benefit depends on topology, workload, software stack, message sizes, overlap, contention, and fallback behavior; counters alone do not establish application improvement.
Memory registration, queue/completion errors, congestion, link faults, or fallback activation can increase tail latency or cause correctness/availability failures.
Telemetry and workload metadata may reveal sensitive information; collect minimum necessary counters, redact payloads, and restrict access.
evidence_required: Recorded topology, GPU/NIC/driver/runtime versions, transport settings, and fallback configuration
Named workload, message-size and parallelism distribution, baseline, warm-up, repetitions, observation windows, and units
Application communication/step-time distributions plus queue, error, link, bandwidth, latency, GPU overlap/utilization, and fallback measurements
Correctness checks, deterministic reproduction, confounder analysis, and rollback-threshold results
